source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Storage drive information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data readable/correct; every storage drive status fits actual status; storage firmware version correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES issues GET on a presumed `/Systems/system/Storage` collection and immediately reads `.Drives`, although drives are normally reached through each Storage member or other advertised links. It flattens only Name, serial and Revision and omits controller/enclosure/slot, protocol, media, capacity, state/health, pagination, field semantics and identifier protection.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly restores complete controller/drive traversal, topology, health/capacity/firmware and a no-mutation boundary, but leaves the finite population/topology/firmware matrix as Pending.

old_problem: A successful flat query or serial/revision list can miss entire storage-controller branches and cannot show which physical bay a drive occupies, whether population and health are correct, or whether `Revision` is authoritative firmware for that device. The previous review found these gaps but treated the Project storage and firmware matrix as an unresolved decision.
disposition_reason: Discover the actual ComputerSystem, traverse every Storage member and all advertised drive relationships/pages, reconcile them with any chassis-level drive collection, and bind each expected physical bay to a protected stable drive identity. Compare complete read-only device/status/capacity/protocol/media and authoritative firmware evidence plus actual WebUI detail against the approved build/firmware matrix. Topology, population and firmware targets are versioned Project execution inputs.
decision_basis: XLSX row 972, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 973 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 973 / variant 8ccd622910ebb050.

DMTF models Storage as a collection of Storage resources and Drive as individual physical-drive resources reachable through advertised relationships; the response `@odata.type` and links govern traversal, so `.Drives` on the collection root is not a portable completeness method.

Drive resources define physical location, capacity, protocol, media, status and Revision fields, but Revision semantics and the approved firmware value remain device/vendor/Project-specific and must be declared before it is used for PASS.

Completeness is topology-based: each expected controller/enclosure/backplane/bay is accounted as populated or intentionally empty, and controller evidence from the next testcase cannot replace this per-drive source identity.

ED-04, ED-08, ED-12, ED-15, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 require protected storage, actual visual evidence, separate firmware verification, approved standards and independent coverage; ED-33 through ED-38 allow Project parameterization and prohibit log deletion, rescan, write I/O, firmware update, reset/power and retry.

test_case.test_name: Validate every expected storage drive's physical identity, status and firmware in BMC inventory
test_case.purpose: Verify the complete expected physical-drive population across every storage controller/enclosure/backplane/bay, including each drive's protected identity, location, model, protocol/media, capacity, state/health and authoritative firmware revision, and reconcile it with actual BMC WebUI detail without issuing storage, firmware or indicator actions.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/system/storage-backplane/controller/firmware/WebUI identity and complete controller-to-enclosure/backplane/bay topology
Approved bay population/build matrix with expected drive model, protocol, media type, capacity/sector rules and protected serial/WWN correlation where applicable
Approved per-model firmware matrix and field authority declaring whether Redfish Drive.Revision, UpdateService inventory or a vendor read-only source establishes firmware
State/health/operational-status, nullable/absent, empty-bay, capacity-unit/tolerance and freshness acceptance rules
Service-root-discovered ComputerSystem Storage collection, every Storage member, advertised Drives/Controllers/chassis-drive relationships and pagination/schema versions
Actual rendered WebUI storage-drive table/detail mapping, trusted TLS/protected credentials, identifier redaction/tokenization, preserved logs and evidence storage
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target and discover the selected ComputerSystem and Storage link; enumerate every Storage member/page, then follow every advertised drive relationship and member link, including documented chassis-level Drive collections, while recording controller/enclosure/backplane/bay ancestry. De-duplicate only by approved durable resource identity and preserve all relationship paths. Build one row for every expected physical bay, including intentionally empty/unsupported bays, and for each present drive record Id/Name, Location/PhysicalLocation/service label, Model/Manufacturer/PartNumber, protected stable serial/WWN token, Protocol, MediaType, CapacityBytes and supported block/sector data, Status.State/Health, operational/indicator state read-only fields, Revision and timestamp/freshness. Resolve firmware using the approved per-model authority; do not assume every Revision string is firmware. Capture the actual rendered WebUI storage-drive table and every required detail and reconcile each bay with the Project matrix and all API views. Preserve baseline and post SEL/audit evidence. Do not clear logs, rescan, create/delete volumes or RAID, run FIO/write I/O, format/erase/sanitize, change indicators, update/downgrade firmware, reset/reboot or power-cycle.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected bay is accounted exactly once as correctly populated or intentionally empty, with no missing, extra, duplicate or misplaced drive. Each installed drive matches approved location, model, protocol/media, capacity/sector rules, acceptable state/health and its per-model authoritative firmware target. Storage-member, drive-resource and actual WebUI views reconcile within freshness tolerance, protected identifiers correlate without disclosure, and storage/controller/system state remains unchanged.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete Storage-member and drive-link/page traversal, every-bay population accounting, topology-backed protected identity, full per-drive attribute and health comparison, authoritative per-model firmware evidence and actual rendered WebUI detail. A collection-level `.Drives`, drive count, Name/Serial/Revision list, controller inventory or aggregate healthy state cannot pass. Missing/extra/misplaced/duplicate drive, wrong model/protocol/media/capacity/firmware, unacceptable or stale status, ambiguous slot, exposed identifier or API/UI/reference mismatch is FAIL. Missing topology, population, firmware authority/target or health semantics is NOT READY rather than Pending; no firmware value or tolerance is guessed.
safety_gate: Use certificate-verified protected GET/read paths discovered from the service; do not assume system ID `system`, a flat Storage shape or one drive relationship is complete.
Bind every observed drive and expected empty bay to approved physical topology; resource order, display name and raw serial alone are not physical-slot proof.
Protect serial, WWN and asset identifiers with stable tokens in shared evidence while retaining an access-controlled raw correlation artifact.
Treat Revision as firmware only under the approved model/schema/vendor rule and compare against the exact approved per-model firmware matrix.
Preserve logs before any deletion; prohibit rescan, volume/RAID mutation, write workload/FIO, format/erase/sanitize, indicator change, firmware flash/downgrade, reset/reboot and power actions.
Stop on incomplete traversal, ambiguous bay, stale/degraded health or mismatch; do not automatically retry through rescan, reset or power transition.
expected_evidence: Immutable target/schema/WebUI identity and approved complete controller/enclosure/backplane/bay population plus firmware matrix
Complete paginated Storage members and all linked Drive/chassis-drive raw artifacts with relationship graph, timestamps and hashes
Per-bay matrix containing expected/observed population, protected identity, model/protocol/media/capacity/sector, state/health, firmware authority/value and verdict
Explicit reconciliation of duplicate resource views and empty/unsupported/absent/inaccessible bay semantics
Actual rendered WebUI storage-drive table and detail visuals with per-bay API/UI/reference comparison
Preserved pre/post logs, no-storage/no-flash/no-reset/no-power audit and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On missing/extra drive, ambiguous bay, stale/degraded health, firmware uncertainty or source disagreement, stop and preserve/redact all inventory, UI and log evidence and obtain the authoritative matrix. Do not clear logs, rescan, alter volumes/RAID, write, format, erase, sanitize, change indicators, flash firmware, reset/reboot, power-cycle or automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: The Master consistently requires every storage drive's details, actual status and firmware. DeepSeek's flat three-field query is incomplete implementation, not a conflicting source intent.

blocked.reason: Read-only per-drive inventory/status/firmware reconciliation is standard and technically defined. Physical topology, population, device-specific firmware targets and health rules are bounded Project inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Controller/enclosure/backplane/bay topology and population; actual advertised resource graph; expected model/protocol/media/capacity/sector rules; per-model firmware authority/targets; status/empty/freshness policy; WebUI mapping; trust and identifier redaction.
